342735.title: The characterization of abelian periods for the slope $[0;\overline{2}]$
342735.statement:
Let $\alpha=[0;\overline{2}]$, and let a **Sturmian word of slope** $\alpha$ be a Sturmian word whose slope is $\alpha$. Denote its abelian period set by the set of positive integers occurring as abelian periods of its factors, and write $\mathcal{Q}^+_{\alpha}$ and $\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}$ for the sets defined in the paper.

**Abelian-period conjecture.** The abelian period set of a Sturmian word of slope $\alpha$ is

$$
\mathcal{Q}^+_{\alpha}\cup\mathcal{M}_{\alpha}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the characterization of all possible abelian periods of factors of a Sturmian word for the specific slope $[0;\overline{2}]$. The surrounding examples show that the possible periods depend heavily on the arithmetic nature of the slope; the proposed description is based on computer experiments.

342741.title: The independence-complex conjecture for products of three complete graphs
342741.statement:
Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $\times$ denote the graph product, and let ${\rm{Ind}}(G)$ denote the independence complex of a graph $G$. For $n\geq 2$, **the independence-complex conjecture.**

$$
{\rm{Ind}}(K_2\times K_3\times K_n)\simeq\bigvee\limits_{(n-1)(3n-2)}\mathbb{S}^3.
$$

This conjecture is based on computer calculations of the Betti numbers for the indicated independence complexes; its resolution would establish the proposed wedge-of-spheres description for this family.

342757.title: Monotonicity of the Robin spectral ratio
342757.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, and let $\lambda_1(\Omega;\alpha)<\lambda_2(\Omega;\alpha)\leq\cdots$ be the Robin eigenvalues for parameter $\alpha\in\mathbb R$.

**Spectral-ratio monotonicity conjecture.** The map

$$
\alpha\mapsto\frac{\lambda_2(\Omega;\alpha)}{\lambda_1(\Omega;\alpha)}
$$

is decreasing for $\alpha>0$.
The conjecture is open even for rectangles; the source notes numerical evidence that it can fail for certain acute isosceles triangles when $\alpha<0$.

342782.title: Universality conjecture for normalized collision times
342782.statement:
Let $T$ be the total time considered above, with expectation and variance denoted by $\mathbb E[T]$ and $\operatorname{Var}(T)$, and let $N$ and $M$ be the parameters satisfying $N \gg M$. Let $\mu$ be a distribution in the stated wide class. **Universality conjecture.** The normalized variable has distribution function

$$
\mathbb P \left( \frac{ T - \mathbb E[T]}{ \sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(T)}} \leq t \right) = 1 - e^{-t-1}.
$$

This predicts a universal limiting law for the relevant stopping time when $N$ dominates $M$; the source does not provide a proof or a resolution, and the intended range of distributions $\mu$ should be checked.

342972.title: Existence of weak signed edge-labelings in 3-connected planar graphs
342972.statement:
Let $H$ be a 3-connected planar graph with an even number of negative vertices. A $\{0,a,b\}$-edge-labeling $c$ is a weak signed edge-labeling if the parity conditions on $d_0(v),d_a(v),d_b(v)$ at positive and negative vertices specified in the paper hold. **Weak signed edge-labeling existence claim.** There exists a weak signed edge-labeling of $H$.

The claim is introduced as an intermediate structural assertion in the reduction from signed vertex-coloring to edge-labeling of a planar dual. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence, and its status as a conjecture rather than a subsequently proved intermediate result should be checked.

342976.title: Hliněný–Kwon–Obdržálek–Ordyniak conjecture on rank-depth
342976.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a class of graphs. A graph $H$ is a **vertex-minor** of a graph $G$ if $H$ can be obtained from $G$ by a sequence of local complementations and vertex deletions. The **rank-depth** of a graph is the parameter discussed above, and a class has bounded rank-depth when its members have rank-depth bounded by a common integer.

**Hliněný–Kwon–Obdržálek–Ordyniak conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{C}$ has bounded rank-depth if and only if there exists an integer $t$ such that no graph $G\in\mathcal{C}$ contains a path of length $t$ as a vertex-minor.

Rank-depth is monotone under taking vertex-minors, making vertex-minor obstructions natural for classes of bounded rank-depth. The conjecture was verified for graphs of rank-width $1$ by Novotný, but remains open in general.

343124.title: Bang–Jensen–Thomassé's arc-connectivity conjecture for supereulerian digraphs
343124.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph. Write $\lambda(D)$ for its arc-connectivity and $\alpha(D)$ for its independence number. A digraph is **supereulerian** if it has a spanning eulerian subdigraph.

**Bang–Jensen–Thomassé's conjecture.** Every digraph $D$ with $\lambda(D)\geq\alpha(D)$ is supereulerian.

This conjecture generalizes Camion's theorem and is open even for digraphs of independence number $2$, although it has been verified for several classes of digraphs.

343210.title: The linear-programming improvement conjecture for Paley graph clique bounds
343210.statement:
Let $G_p$ be the Paley graph for a prime $p\equiv 1~(\operatorname{mod}4)$, let $\operatorname{LS}(p)$ denote the linear programming bound obtained in the paper, and let $\operatorname{HP}(p)$ denote the Hanson--Petridis bound. **Linear-programming improvement conjecture.** For infinitely many primes $p\equiv 1~(\operatorname{mod}4)$, one has

$$
\operatorname{LS}(p)<\lfloor \operatorname{HP}(p)\rfloor.
$$

The numerical experiments suggest that this linear programming bound sometimes improves on the best known closed-form Hanson--Petridis bound; proving infinitely many such improvements remains open.

343244.title: Optimal strong approximation conjecture for the four-square form
343244.statement:
Let $N,m,\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_4\in\mathbb{Z}$ satisfy

$$
N\equiv\sum_{i=1}^4\lambda_i^2\pmod m.
$$
 **Four-square strong approximation conjecture.** If $N\gg m^{4+\varepsilon}$, then there exists $(x_1,\dots,x_4)\in\mathbb{Z}^4$ such that

$$
\sum_{i=1}^4x_i^2=N,
$$

and

$$
x_l\equiv\lambda_l\pmod m\qquad(1\leq l\leq4).
$$

This is the integral four-variable conjecture whose function-field analogue would yield the sharp upper bound for LPS Ramanujan graph diameters; the source presents it as an optimal strong-approximation conjecture and gives numerical evidence elsewhere.

343471.title: The 3-adic valuation pattern conjecture for Morse link numbers
343471.statement:
Let $L_n$ denote the Morse link numbers, and let $\xi_3$ denote the 3-adic valuation. For odd $n\geq 3$, if $\alpha$ is a 3-adic integer, define the final ternary digit of the unit part of $n-\alpha$ by

$$
\frac{n-\alpha}{3^{\xi_3(n-\alpha)}}.
$$

This digit is $1$ or $2$.

**3-adic valuation pattern conjecture.** There exists a 3-adic integer $\alpha$ such that, for odd $n\geq 3$, the quantity $\xi_3(L_n-1)$ depends only on $\xi_3(n-\alpha)$ and the last digit of

$$
\frac{n-\alpha}{3^{\xi_3(n-\alpha)}}.
$$

The claim is motivated by computational evidence, and the source explicitly says that the pattern may be more complicated than the analogous 5-adic conjecture; no resolution is supplied.

343472.title: Non-algebraicity conjecture for generating functions of non-super-strict partitions
343472.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a strict partition. It is **super-strict** if no two nonzero parts of $\mu$ differ by $1$.

**Non-algebraicity conjecture.** If $\mu$ is not super-strict, meaning that $\mu$ contains two nonzero parts which differ by $1$, then the generating function for $\mu$ is not algebraic.

The conjecture concerns the algebraic nature of generating functions enumerating pattern-avoiding integer partitions. The paper states that the corresponding generating functions are in fact known to be non-algebraic in this setting, but the parser supplies no resolution status for the conjecture; this status should be checked against the paper's surrounding results.

343489.title: Engel et al.'s antichain Hausdorff-measure conjecture
343489.statement:
Let $[0,1]^n$ be equipped with the coordinatewise partial order, and let an **antichain** be a subset $A\subset[0,1]^n$ containing no two distinct comparable points. Write $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(A)$ for its $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. **Engel et al.'s conjecture.** There exists an antichain $A$ in $[0,1]^n$ such that

$$
\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(A)=n.
$$

The bound $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(A)\leq n$ is known, and it is asymptotically sharp; the conjecture is verified for $n=1$ and $n=2$, but its validity in general remains open.

343506.title: Containment conjecture for cyclic-prime shuffle groups
343506.statement:
Let $k$ be an odd prime, let $n>k$, and suppose that $n$ is not a power of $k$. **Cyclic-prime shuffle-group conjecture.** Then

$$
\mathrm{Sh}(C_k,n)\supseteq\mathrm{Alt}(kn).
$$

This is presented as a computationally verified expectation for the cyclic case and as a property that should follow from the broader generalised-shuffle-group conjecture. No proof or disproof is supplied in the source.

343628.title: Conjecture on minimally _g-imperfect graphs
343628.statement: Let $G$ be a graph. It is **minimally $\gamma_g$-imperfect** if $G$ is not $\gamma_g$-perfect, while every proper induced subgraph of $G$ is $\gamma_g$-perfect. The anti-holes $\overline{C_n}$ for $n\geq 5$, together with the eight additional graphs listed in Proposition~, are the graphs under consideration. **Classification conjecture.** There are no other minimally $\gamma_g$-imperfect graphs but those listed in Proposition~. This conjecture is based on computer verification for graphs with at most nine vertices and on the paper's structural results for connected and triangle-free imperfect graphs; its status beyond those verified cases remains open.

343646.title: Discreteness conjecture for non-even p-frame energy minimizers
343646.statement:
Let $p>0$ with $p\notin 2\mathbb N$, and let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$. Its $p$-frame energy is

$$
I_f(\mu)=\int_{\mathbb S^{d-1}}\int_{\mathbb S^{d-1}}|\langle x,y\rangle|^p\,d\mu(x)d\mu(y).
$$

A **finite discrete measure** is a measure supported on finitely many points. **Discreteness conjecture.** Every minimizer of $I_f$ is a finite discrete measure on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$. For even integer $p$, continuous and discrete minimizers are plentiful, whereas for non-even $p$ the asserted discreteness is supported by results for tight designs and numerical evidence; the conjecture remains open in general.

343796.title: Generic polygon invariance conjecture for higher associahedra
343796.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the set of vertices of a **generic** convex $n$-gon, and let $\Upsigma_{\mathcal{A},k}$ be the associated higher associahedron. The **generic polygon invariance conjecture.** The $f$-vector of $\Upsigma_{\mathcal{A},k}$ depends only on $n$ and $k$. This would extend the combinatorial invariance of the ordinary associahedron to higher associahedra for generic convex polygons, despite the dependence on the point configuration in the nongeneric setting. The claim is supported in the source by computational evidence, but no resolution is given.

344002.title: The uniqueness conjecture for extreme subsets of prime cyclic groups
344002.statement:
Let $p$ be prime and let $A$ be an $n$-element subset of the cyclic group $\mathbb Z_p$, where $1<n<p$. Two subsets are **equivalent** in the sense used by the paper's classification of extreme sets.

**Prime-cyclic uniqueness conjecture.** All extreme $n$-element subsets of $\mathbb Z_p$ are equivalent.

The conjecture is suggested by the observed examples and numerical evidence concerning extreme sets in cyclic groups. No resolution is supplied in the given text, so it remains open.

344003.title: The differing-Sidon-constant criterion for extreme subsets
344003.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of the cyclic group $\mathbb Z_k$. Assume that $A$ and $B$ have the same cardinality and the same Sidon constant, but belong to different equivalence classes.

**Differing-Sidon-constant conjecture.** Under these assumptions, $A$ and $B$ are extreme.

This claim is motivated by the paper's examples and numerical evidence about equivalence classes and Sidon constants. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the assertion remains open.

344004.title: The prime-cardinality frequency conjecture for extreme sets
344004.statement:
Consider the frequency with which extreme sets occur, grouped by the cardinality of the sets. A cardinality is **prime** when it is a prime integer, and it is a perfect square when it has the form $m^2$ for an integer $m$.

**Prime-cardinality frequency conjecture.** Extreme sets with prime cardinality appear more frequently than sets whose cardinality is neither prime nor a perfect square.

This is a qualitative conjecture based on examples and numerical evidence rather than a stated quantitative frequency measure. The supplied text gives no resolution, so it remains open.

344302.title: The down-up-down-up conjecture for singleton double descent counts
344302.statement: Let $dd(I;n)$ denote the number of permutations in the symmetric group on $n$ letters whose double descent set is $I$. Given a fixed $n\in\mathbb{N}$, **the down-up-down-up conjecture** asserts that for $2\leq i<\left\lceil\frac n2\right\rceil$, $dd(\{i\};n)>dd(\{i+1\};n)$ when $i$ is even, and $dd(\{i\};n)<dd(\{i+1\};n)$ when $i$ is odd. The pattern has been numerically verified for some values of $n$ and is conjectured to persist generally.
